intro: On the Aksaray–Nevşehir road, in Aksaray province, stands Ağzıkarahan Caravanserai, built in 1231–1239. With its kiosk mosque at the centre of the court, this Seljuk han is a smaller, plainer sibling of the Sultan Han. Imagine the caravans arriving at its gate.
history: The han was built in two campaigns: first the covered hall in 1231, then the courtyard and portal in 1239. For caravans on the Aksaray–Nevşehir road, it was the next stop after the Sultan Han. Now look at the kiosk mosque at the centre of the court. It stands on four piers, high enough for loaded camels to pass beneath.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the portal, the kiosk mosque, the covered hall and the courtyard arcades.
facts: Did you know? Seljuk hans were set a day's camel march apart, thirty to forty kilometres, and the gap between Ağzıkarahan and the Sultan Han is exactly that. And the kiosk mosque at the centre of the court stands on four piers, high enough for loaded camels to pass right beneath it.
outro: This brings our journey through Ağzıkarahan Caravanserai to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
